passages: [prose] Among the trophic type functional traits (TT_FT), Epigaeic omnivores (EO), comprising 4441 individuals and 37 species, followed by Epigaeic predators (EP) with 1748 individuals and 18 species, dominated in terms of abundance and richness. Conversely, Cryptic predators (CP) with 12 individuals and five species and Leaf-cutting Attini (LA) and Arboreal dominants (AD) (73 and 74 individuals and seven and five species, respectively) were less abundant and relatively poorer in diversity. [table 4] Functional traits | Trait specificity | Description
Ecosystem specificity (ES_FT) | Forest specialists (FS) | Species exclusively captured in primary (PF) or secondary forests (SF).
Open and semi-open environment specialists (OS) | Species exclusively captured in pastures (PA) and cocoa agroforests (AG).
Forest generalists (FG) | Species captured in forests (PF and SF)
Ecosystem generalists (EG) | Species captured in all ecosystems
Trophic type (TT_FT) | Cryptic Predators (CP) | Small species that nest primarily in the soil, leaf and rotting logs, where they specialize on living arthropods or their eggs
Cryptic Omnivores (CO) | Small species nesting within the soil, leaf and rotting logs, where they are generalist predators and scavengers
Epigaeic Predators (EP) | Medium-to large-sized species that forage on the litter surface and are specialist predators of other arthropods
Epigaeic Omnivores (EO) | Medium-to large-sized species that forage on the litter surface and are generalist predators and scavengers
Arboreal Dominants (AD) | Highly active and aggressive species with large colony sizes, nesting in trees
